records.context: A bounded five-second join used to let the screen disappear while the daemon independent execution path still owned a live SQLite connection.  That is unsafe at application shutdown: CPython can finalize the sqlite extension while the independent execution path is still inside it.  SQLite already bounds lock waits with its 30-second connection timeout, so a requested blocking stop waits for the independent execution path to close its cursor and connection completely.
records.label: spacr.qt.annotate_engine.SaveWorker.stop#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A bounded five-second join used to let the screen disappear while the daemon thread still owned a live SQLite connection.  That is unsafe at application shutdown: CPython can finalize the sqlite extension while the thread is still inside it.  SQLite already bounds lock waits with its 30-second connection timeout, so a requested blocking stop waits for the thread to close its cursor and connection completely.
records.translation: En tidsbegränsad väntan på fem sekunder lät tidigare skärmen försvinna medan daemontråden fortfarande ägde en aktiv SQLite-anslutning.  Det är osäkert vid programavstängning: CPython kan slutföra sqlite-tillägget medan tråden fortfarande befinner sig i det.  SQLite begränsar redan väntan på lås med sin tidsgräns på 30 sekunder för anslutningen, så ett begärt blockerande stopp väntar tills tråden helt har stängt sin markör och anslutning.

records.context: Compared with ``==``, not ``is``. The pattern this module documents — ``register_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in the constructor and ``unregister_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in ``closeEvent`` — hands over a *different bound-method object* each time, because Python builds a new one on every attribute access. Under an identity check that made every withdrawal a silent no-op, so the process-wide registry kept a reference to a destroyed application view and the next ``open_objects`` reached it. Bound methods compare equal exactly when their ``__self__`` and ``__func__`` match, which is the question being asked; anything that does not define ``__eq__`` (a lambda, a ``partial``) still falls back to identity, so the two-application view guarantee above is unchanged.

records.source: Three decisions make the result usable:
records.translation: Tre beslut gör resultatet användbart:

records.context: **Only the objects the line actually crosses are touched.** The cut is clipped to them, so a line drawn past a neighbour leaves that neighbour's every pixel where it was. (The standalone tool relabels the whole microscope field of view after cutting, which renumbers every other object in it — the same re-keying :func:`canonical_labels` exists to avoid.)

records.source: **Only the objects the line actually crosses are touched.** The cut is clipped to them, so a line drawn past a neighbour leaves that neighbour's every pixel where it was. (The standalone tool relabels the whole field after cutting, which renumbers every other object in it — the same re-keying :func:`canonical_labels` exists to avoid.)
records.translation: **Endast de objekt som linjen faktiskt korsar berörs.** Snittet klipps till dem, så en linje som dras förbi en granne lämnar varje pixel hos den grannen där den var. (Det fristående verktyget etiketterar om hela bildfältet efter snittet, vilket numrerar om varje annat objekt i det — samma omnyckling som :func:`canonical_labels` finns för att undvika.)

records.context: **The larger piece keeps the original id**, and the smaller pieces get fresh ones above the mask's top label. That is the rule :func:`canonical_labels` already applies when one id names two blobs, so dividing and then saving does not renumber anything, and the id stays on the piece that carries most of what it used to name.

records.translation: **Den större delen behåller det ursprungliga id:t**, och de mindre delarna får nya över maskens högsta etikett. Det är den regel som :func:`canonical_labels` redan tillämpar när ett id anger två fläckar, så att dela och sedan spara numrerar inte om något, och id:t stannar på den del som bär det mesta av det som det tidigare angav.

records.context: the session's :class:`spacr.curation.CurationLog` for this microscope field of view. Given one holding at least one edit, it is written to ``<mask>.curation.json`` beside the mask, so :func:`spacr.curation.is_curated` reports the saved mask as hand-edited. The log is written whole, so it must have been seeded from :meth:`CurationLog.read_beside` to keep earlier sessions' entries -- which is what the screen does on load. A log with no edits writes no sidecar: a session that opened the editor and painted nothing has not curated anything, and a ledger that exists for every mask ever opened answers no question.

A log with no edits writes no sidecar: a session that opened the editor and painted nothing has not curated anything, and a ledger that exists for every mask ever opened answers no question.
records.translation: sessionens :class:`spacr.curation.CurationLog` för det här bildfältet. Om den innehåller minst en redigering skrivs den till ``<mask>.curation.json`` bredvid masken, så att :func:`spacr.curation.is_curated` rapporterar den sparade masken som handredigerad. Loggen skrivs i sin helhet, så den måste ha initierats från :meth:`CurationLog.read_beside` för att behålla tidigare sessioners poster -- vilket är vad skärmen gör vid inläsning. En logg utan redigeringar skriver ingen sidofil: en session som öppnade redigeraren och inte målade något har inte kurerat något, och en liggare som finns för varje mask som någonsin öppnats besvarar ingen fråga.

records.translation: Att ge nyckeln ett standardvärde för measure på samma sätt som appen Mask gör skulle inte åtgärda detta, av två skäl som måste åtgärdas tillsammans.

records.context: So the demo deliberately omits the key, and the wiring needed elsewhere is: widen ``expected_types['summarize_organelles_by']`` to ``(str, list, type(None))``; make ``get_measure_crop_settings`` default it to ``['cell', 'organelle']`` (safe — every write is separately gated on ``organelle_mask_dim is not None``, which defaults to ``None``); and add it to the ``measure`` section of ``spacr/qt/screens/settings_model.py`` so the Measure form can hold it — without a widget, ``apply_settings_dict`` drops it and ``collect()`` never emits it, so a CSV key would change what a CLI run measures and nothing about a GUI processing session.

records.translation: Datamängden och inställningarna som detta skriver klarar förkontrollen, men *pipelinen* för Timelapse kan fortfarande inte konsumera dem, och inget av felen ligger i den här modulen. Båda återskapades på det här demot och båda korrigeringarna bevisades genom att patcha de två funktionerna vid körning; med paret tillämpat slutförs demot och skriver 8 sammanslagna stackar, filmer per kanal, en GIF med spåröverlägg och en ``tracks/*.csv`` med 16 spår.

records.context: 1. ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files`` names its stack files ``<plate>_<well>_<field>.npy`` when ``timelapse=True`` — dropping the timeID and max-projecting every timepoint of a microscope field of view into one array — while ``spacr.io._generate_time_lists`` groups on ``<plate>_<well>_<field>_<time>.npy`` and skips anything with fewer than four underscore-separated parts. An 8-frame microscope field of view becomes one ``stack/plate1_A01_1.npy``, ``_generate_time_lists`` returns ``[]``, no ``*_norm_timelapse.npz`` is written, no masks are generated, and ``preprocess_generate_masks`` dies in ``_pivot_counts_table`` on ``no such table: object_counts``. Emitting the timeID in both branches (the non-timelapse spelling is already exactly what ``_generate_time_lists`` parses) is the fix. 2. Past that, ``spacr.object.generate_cellpose_masks_sam`` hands ``spacr.timelapse._trackpy_track_cells`` a **list** of 2-D frames, and the tracking chain indexes it as an array: ``_track_by_iou`` does ``masks.shape[0]`` and ``_relabel_masks_based_on_tracks`` does ``np.zeros(masks.shape, …)``, both ``AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'``. In the ``timelapse_mode='iou'`` path this demo asks for, the first one is swallowed by the ``except Exception`` retry loop in ``_facilitate_trackin_with_adaptive_removal``, which then shrinks the search range 100 times and reports ``Failed to track after 100 attempts`` — a message about displacement for a bug about a type. Coercing once at the top of ``_trackpy_track_cells`` (``masks = np.asarray(masks)``) clears both.
records.label: spacr.qt.synthetic.generate_timelapse_demo#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files`` names its stack files ``<plate>_<well>_<field>.npy`` when ``timelapse=True`` — dropping the timeID and max-projecting every timepoint of a field into one array — while ``spacr.io._generate_time_lists`` groups on ``<plate>_<well>_<field>_<time>.npy`` and skips anything with fewer than four underscore-separated parts. An 8-frame field becomes one ``stack/plate1_A01_1.npy``, ``_generate_time_lists`` returns ``[]``, no ``*_norm_timelapse.npz`` is written, no masks are generated, and ``preprocess_generate_masks`` dies in ``_pivot_counts_table`` on ``no such table: object_counts``. Emitting the timeID in both branches (the non-timelapse spelling is already exactly what ``_generate_time_lists`` parses) is the fix. 2. Past that, ``spacr.object.generate_cellpose_masks_sam`` hands ``spacr.timelapse._trackpy_track_cells`` a **list** of 2-D frames, and the tracking chain indexes it as an array: ``_track_by_iou`` does ``masks.shape[0]`` and ``_relabel_masks_based_on_tracks`` does ``np.zeros(masks.shape, …)``, both ``AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'``. In the ``timelapse_mode='iou'`` path this demo asks for, the first one is swallowed by the ``except Exception`` retry loop in ``_facilitate_trackin_with_adaptive_removal``, which then shrinks the search range 100 times and reports ``Failed to track after 100 attempts`` — a message about displacement for a bug about a type. Coercing once at the top of ``_trackpy_track_cells`` (``masks = np.asarray(masks)``) clears both.
records.translation: 1. ``spacr.io._rename_and_organize_image_files`` namnger sina stackfiler ``<plate>_<well>_<field>.npy`` när ``timelapse=True`` — vilket tappar timeID och maxprojicerar varje tidpunkt i ett bildfält till en enda matris — medan ``spacr.io._generate_time_lists`` grupperar på ``<plate>_<well>_<field>_<time>.npy`` och hoppar över allt med färre än fyra delar separerade av understreck. Ett bildfält med 8 bildrutor blir en enda ``stack/plate1_A01_1.npy``, ``_generate_time_lists`` returnerar ``[]``, ingen ``*_norm_timelapse.npz`` skrivs, inga masker genereras, och ``preprocess_generate_masks`` dör i ``_pivot_counts_table`` på ``no such table: object_counts``. Att skriva ut timeID i båda grenarna (stavningen utan timelapse är redan exakt vad ``_generate_time_lists`` tolkar) är korrigeringen. 2. Därefter lämnar ``spacr.object.generate_cellpose_masks_sam`` en **lista** med 2-D-bildrutor till ``spacr.timelapse._trackpy_track_cells``, och spårningskedjan indexerar den som en matris: ``_track_by_iou`` gör ``masks.shape[0]`` och ``_relabel_masks_based_on_tracks`` gör ``np.zeros(masks.shape, …)``, båda ``AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'``. I den väg med ``timelapse_mode='iou'`` som det här demot begär sväljs det första av omförsöksloopen med ``except Exception`` i ``_facilitate_trackin_with_adaptive_removal``, som sedan krymper sökintervallet 100 gånger och rapporterar ``Failed to track after 100 attempts`` — ett meddelande om förflyttning för en bugg om en typ. Att konvertera en gång överst i ``_trackpy_track_cells`` (``masks = np.asarray(masks)``) åtgärdar båda.

records.context: Re-entrant calls on the same thread are refused. Drawing a line runs Python inside a QWidget, and with verbose logging on the function-trace profile hook logs on entry to every spaCR function it passes through — including this one. Both console log sinks feed that record straight back here, and ``_StdoutBlock.append`` answers it with a nested ``setPlainText`` whose first act is to destroy the QTextDocument's frames — the ones the outer call is still inside. gdb: ``QTextFrame::~QTextFrame -> QTextDocumentPrivate::clear``, ``#0`` in freed memory. Reproduced as ``pytest tests/qt/test_all_module_smoke.py tests/qt/test_batch_f_diagnostics.py`` (exit 139).
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.console_panel.ConsolePanel.append_stdout#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Re-entrant calls on the same thread are refused. Drawing a line runs Python inside a QWidget, and with verbose logging on the function-trace profile hook logs on entry to every spaCR function it passes through — including this one. Both console log sinks feed that record straight back here, and ``_StdoutBlock.append`` answers it with a nested ``setPlainText`` whose first act is to destroy the QTextDocument's frames — the ones the outer call is still inside. gdb: ``QTextFrame::~QTextFrame -> QTextDocumentPrivate::clear``, ``#0`` in freed memory. Reproduced as ``pytest tests/qt/test_all_module_smoke.py tests/qt/test_batch_f_diagnostics.py`` (exit 139).
records.translation: Återinträdande anrop på samma tråd vägras. Att rita en rad kör Python inuti en QWidget, och med utförlig loggning på loggar profilkroken för funktionsspårning vid inträde i varje spaCR-funktion den passerar — inklusive den här. Båda konsolens loggmottagare matar den posten direkt tillbaka hit, och ``_StdoutBlock.append`` svarar med en nästlad ``setPlainText`` vars första åtgärd är att förstöra ramarna i QTextDocument — de som det yttre anropet fortfarande befinner sig i. gdb: ``QTextFrame::~QTextFrame -> QTextDocumentPrivate::clear``, ``#0`` i frigjort minne. Återskapat som ``pytest tests/qt/test_all_module_smoke.py tests/qt/test_batch_f_diagnostics.py`` (avslutningskod 139).

records.context: Cancel any active stream and block until its QThread has exited. Must be called before the panel (or its parent window) is destroyed — otherwise Python drops the last reference to the executing QThread and Qt aborts with: `QThread: Destroyed while thread '' is still running`.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.console_panel.ConsolePanel.shutdown#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Cancel any active stream and block until its QThread has exited. Must be called before the panel (or its parent window) is destroyed — otherwise Python drops the last reference to the running QThread and Qt aborts with: `QThread: Destroyed while thread '' is still running`.
records.translation: Avbryter eventuell aktiv ström och blockerar tills dess QThread har avslutats. Måste anropas innan panelen (eller dess överordnade fönster) förstörs — annars släpper Python den sista referensen till den körande QThread och Qt avbryter med: `QThread: Destroyed while thread '' is still running`.

records.context: There is deliberately no ``QThread.terminate()`` fallback. It used to be here, described as a last resort, and it was reached far more often than "last resort" suggests: `spacr.qt.ai.worker` queued `worker.finished -> thread.quit` to the GUI-affine QThread object, so the event that stops the independent execution path sat behind this method's own `wait()` and the wait timed out on streams that had already finished. Terminating an independent execution path that is executing Python is `pthread_cancel`: if it dies holding the GIL the process stops making progress with every independent execution path still alive, and if it dies inside Qt or PySide the heap is corrupt and the crash lands somewhere unrelated later. `bridge.drain_thread` parks an independent execution path that will not stop instead, which keeps the "never destroy an executing QThread" rule without buying it with undefined behaviour.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.console_panel.ConsolePanel.shutdown#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: There is deliberately no ``QThread.terminate()`` fallback. It used to be here, described as a last resort, and it was reached far more often than "last resort" suggests: `spacr.qt.ai.worker` queued `worker.finished -> thread.quit` to the GUI-affine QThread object, so the event that stops the thread sat behind this method's own `wait()` and the wait timed out on streams that had already finished. Terminating a thread that is running Python is `pthread_cancel`: if it dies holding the GIL the process stops making progress with every thread still alive, and if it dies inside Qt or PySide the heap is corrupt and the crash lands somewhere unrelated later. `bridge.drain_thread` parks a thread that will not stop instead, which keeps the "never destroy a running QThread" rule without buying it with undefined behaviour.
records.translation: Det finns avsiktligt ingen reserv med ``QThread.terminate()``. Den fanns tidigare här, beskriven som en sista utväg, och den nåddes betydligt oftare än "last resort" (sista utväg) antyder: `spacr.qt.ai.worker` köade `worker.finished -> thread.quit` till QThread-objektet med GUI-affinitet, så händelsen som stoppar tråden låg bakom den här metodens egen `wait()` och väntan löpte ut för strömmar som redan var klara. Att avsluta en tråd som kör Python med våld är `pthread_cancel`: om den dör medan den håller GIL slutar processen göra framsteg med varje tråd fortfarande vid liv, och om den dör inuti Qt eller PySide är heapen skadad och kraschen inträffar senare någonstans orelaterat. `bridge.drain_thread` parkerar i stället en tråd som inte vill stanna, vilket bevarar regeln "never destroy a running QThread" utan att köpa den med odefinierat beteende.

records.context: The first "→ Starting ..." notice of a session cost 33 ms on the main GUI execution path, almost all of it Qt looking up a fallback font for the arrow at the console's size; the same text costs 0.5 ms after that. The lookup is cached per independent execution path and per size, so it can only be done here, on the main GUI execution path, ahead of the notice: a processing session waiting on its workflow's import calls this while the busy bar is already showing. The font is taken from a stand-in entry, because the one an entry draws with carries the family list its sheet gives it, and a font that differs only in that list is a different cache entry.

records.source: The first "→ Starting ..." notice of a session cost 33 ms on the GUI thread, almost all of it Qt looking up a fallback font for the arrow at the console's size; the same text costs 0.5 ms after that. The lookup is cached per thread and per size, so it can only be done here, on the GUI thread, ahead of the notice: a Run waiting on its pipeline's import calls this while the busy bar is already showing. The font is taken from a stand-in entry, because the one an entry draws with carries the family list its sheet gives it, and a font that differs only in that list is a different cache entry.
records.translation: Sessionens första meddelande "→ Starting ..." kostade 33 ms på GUI-tråden, nästan allt Qt som letade upp ett reservteckensnitt för pilen i konsolens storlek; samma text kostar 0.5 ms därefter. Uppslagningen cachas per tråd och per storlek, så den kan bara göras här, på GUI-tråden, före meddelandet: en Run som väntar på sin pipelines import anropar detta medan upptaget-raden redan visas. Teckensnittet hämtas från en ersättningspost, eftersom det som en post ritar med bär den familjelista som dess formatmall ger det, och ett teckensnitt som bara skiljer sig i den listan är en annan cachepost.

records.context: The target is a misiurewicz point, preperiod 4 period 1, refined at startup by solving ``f_c^5(0) = f_c^4(0)``. It has to be ON the boundary: an interior point fades to flat colour as you descend into it and an exterior one escapes, and either way the zoom stops finding anything. A boundary point keeps revealing structure at any magnification.

records.translation: MÅLET ÄR EN MISIUREWICZ-PUNKT, förperiod 4 period 1, förfinad vid start genom att lösa ``f_c^5(0) = f_c^4(0)``. Den måste ligga PÅ randen: en inre punkt bleknar till platt färg när man går ned i den och en yttre flyr, och i båda fallen slutar zoomningen att hitta något. records.context: A plain object with no qt in it, on purpose. This logic used to live inside the GPU canvas's `__init__`, which meant it could only be exercised by building a GL context -- so every claim about how smooth it was came from a SIMULATION written beside it rather than from the code that runs. Three "fixed" reports in a row were wrong that way. Here the real thing can be driven frame by frame and measured.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.fractal_mandelbrot.SteeringCamera#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A PLAIN OBJECT WITH NO QT IN IT, on purpose. This logic used to live inside the GPU canvas's `__init__`, which meant it could only be exercised by building a GL context -- so every claim about how smooth it was came from a SIMULATION written beside it rather than from the code that runs. Three "fixed" reports in a row were wrong that way. Here the real thing can be driven frame by frame and measured.
records.translation: ETT ENKELT OBJEKT UTAN QT, avsiktligt. Den här logiken låg tidigare inuti GPU-dukens `__init__`, vilket innebar att den bara kunde provas genom att bygga en GL-kontext -- så varje påstående om hur jämn den var kom från en SIMULERING som skrivits bredvid den snarare än från den kod som körs. Tre rapporter i rad om att det var "fixed" (åtgärdat) var fel på det sättet. Här kan den verkliga koden drivas bildruta för bildruta och mätas.

records.context: The camera follows; it does not make moves. Easing from A to B over a few seconds and then holding until the next target is chosen makes the picture slide, stop, slide, stop -- and that alternation is what reads as jerking. Instead it eases toward wherever the target currently is at a constant rate: choosing a new target moves the target, and nothing starts or stops.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.fractal_mandelbrot.SteeringCamera#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: THE CAMERA FOLLOWS; IT DOES NOT MAKE MOVES. Easing from A to B over a few seconds and then holding until the next target is chosen makes the picture slide, stop, slide, stop -- and that alternation is what reads as jerking. Instead it eases toward wherever the target currently is at a constant rate: choosing a new target moves the target, and nothing starts or stops.
records.translation: KAMERAN FÖLJER; DEN GÖR INGA FÖRFLYTTNINGAR. Att mjukt röra sig från A till B under några sekunder och sedan stå still tills nästa mål väljs får bilden att glida, stanna, glida, stanna -- och den växlingen är det som uppfattas som ryckighet. I stället rör den sig mjukt mot det ställe där målet för närvarande finns, med konstant hastighet: att välja ett nytt mål flyttar målet, och ingenting startar eller stannar.

records.source: CHECKED BEFORE THE GPU WIDGET IS BUILT, because getting it wrong does not raise. On the `offscreen` platform Qt prints "QOpenGLWidget is not supported on this platform" and the process DUMPS CORE -- which no `except` around the constructor can catch, so the fallback in `create_fractal_widget` would never run. Every test and every headless launch is that platform.
records.translation: KONTROLLERAS INNAN GPU-WIDGETEN BYGGS, eftersom ett fel här inte utlöser något undantag. På plattformen `offscreen` skriver Qt ut "QOpenGLWidget is not supported on this platform" och processen GÖR EN KÄRNDUMP -- vilket inget `except` kring konstruktorn kan fånga, så reserven i `create_fractal_widget` skulle aldrig köras. Varje test och varje start utan skärm sker på den plattformen.

records.context: Categorical series take a fixed eight-hue order — never cycled, never re-assigned when a filter changes the series count, so a gene keeps its colour between two charts. The order is the validated reference palette (light and dark steps kept separately rather than flipped), and a continuous colour column gets a single-hue light-to-dark ramp. records.translation: Kategoriska serier får en fast ordning med åtta nyanser — aldrig cyklisk, aldrig omtilldelad när ett filter ändrar antalet serier, så att en gen behåller sin färg mellan två diagram. records.source: Almost always ``(spec.x, spec.y)``. Without this the scales would be computed for an axis nothing is drawn on, panels would autoscale independently, and a faceted "histogram of Y" would quietly stop sharing its bins.
records.translation: Nästan alltid ``(spec.x, spec.y)``. Undantaget är en ensam kolumn på Y som härleder ett histogram eller ett stapeldiagram: de ritar kolumnen längs den horisontella axeln och antalen uppåt längs den vertikala, oavsett i vilken zon den släpptes. Utan detta skulle skalorna beräknas för en axel som ingenting ritas på, panelerna skulle skala automatiskt var för sig, och ett fasetterat "histogram of Y" (histogram över Y) skulle i tysthet sluta dela sina staplar.

records.context: The order is why this parameter is here rather than in :func:`numpy_to_qpixmap`. The primaries are an image data channel-to-colour mapping and only image data channels belong in it. An outline is not an image data channel -- it is a colour the user chose, or a categorical label -- so putting it through the same matrix would answer a request for a red outline with a yellow one. Recolour the image, then draw on top.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.overlay_masks#9
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The order is why this parameter is here rather than in :func:`numpy_to_qpixmap`. The primaries are a channel-to-colour mapping and only channels belong in it. An outline is not a channel -- it is a colour the user chose, or a categorical label -- so putting it through the same matrix would answer a request for a red outline with a yellow one. Recolour the image, then draw on top.
records.translation: Ordningen är skälet till att den här parametern finns här och inte i :func:`numpy_to_qpixmap`. Primärfärgerna är en avbildning från kanal till färg och endast kanaler hör hemma i den. En kontur är ingen kanal -- den är en färg som användaren valde, eller en kategorisk etikett -- så att skicka den genom samma matris skulle besvara en begäran om en röd kontur med en gul. Färga om bilden och rita sedan ovanpå.

records.context: A NaN in a spaCR measurement table is usually *structural*, not missing at random — the same reasoning :mod:`spacr.anndata_export` sets out at length. A ``pathogen_*`` column is NaN for a cell with no pathogen in it; that is a fact about the cell, not a gap in the record. Mean-imputing it invents a pathogen of average size and moves an uninfected cell into the middle of the infected distribution, invisibly.

records.translation: Ett NaN i en spaCR-mättabell är oftast *strukturellt*, inte slumpmässigt saknat — samma resonemang som :mod:`spacr.anndata_export` utvecklar utförligt. En ``pathogen_*``-kolumn är NaN för en cell utan patogen i sig; det är ett faktum om cellen, inte en lucka i posten. Att imputera den med medelvärdet hittar på en patogen av genomsnittlig storlek och flyttar en oinfekterad cell in i mitten av den infekterade fördelningen, osynligt.

records.context: :data:`NAN_AUTO`, the default, picks between the first two by how the missingness is shaped, because in this table the two shapes are far apart: a structural NaN affects tens of percent of the rows (every uninfected cell), a sporadic one affects a handful (one object where mahotas returned nothing). So a feature missing in more than :data:`DEFAULT_STRUCTURAL_MISSING` of the rows is treated as structural and dropped by name; rows still carrying a NaN among the survivors are dropped as sporadic and counted. Nothing is imputed, and both actions appear in :attr:`PCAResult.notes` and in :meth:`PCAResult.report`.

records.context: A **constant** column has SD 0, so standardising it is 0/0. Left in, it contributes a NaN that spreads through the whole decomposition; "fixed" by substituting a 1, it becomes a zero-variance direction that the solver is free to return as a component with an arbitrary loading pattern. It is dropped before the decomposition and named in :attr:`PCAResult.dropped_features` — a column with one value cannot explain variation in anything.

records.translation: En **konstant** kolumn har SD 0, så att standardisera den är 0/0. Om den lämnas kvar bidrar den med ett NaN som sprider sig genom hela uppdelningen; "fixed" (åtgärdad) genom att ersättas med en 1:a blir den en riktning med noll varians som lösaren fritt kan returnera som en komponent med ett godtyckligt laddningsmönster. records.context: PCA maximises variance, and variance has units. In a spaCR object table ``cell_area`` is px² and runs to 10^4 with a variance near 10^6; ``eccentricity`` is dimensionless and lives in ``[0, 1]``; ``channel_1_mean_intensity`` is counts. An unscaled (covariance) PCA of those three returns "PC1 = cell_area" every time — not because size is the interesting axis but because px² is a big number. Worse, the answer is not even stable: recording the same areas in µm² instead of px² would rotate every component.

records.source: PCA maximises variance, and variance has units. An unscaled (covariance) PCA of those three returns "PC1 = cell_area" every time — not because size is the interesting axis but because px² is a big number. Worse, the answer is not even stable: recording the same areas in µm² instead of px² would rotate every component.
records.translation: PCA maximerar varians, och varians har enheter. I en spaCR-objekttabell är ``cell_area`` i px² och når 10^4 med en varians nära 10^6; ``eccentricity`` är dimensionslös och ligger i ``[0, 1]``; ``channel_1_mean_intensity`` är antal. En oskalad (kovarians-)PCA av de tre returnerar "PC1 = cell_area" varje gång — inte för att storlek är den intressanta axeln utan för att px² är ett stort tal. Värre är att svaret inte ens är stabilt: att registrera samma areor i µm² i stället för px² skulle rotera varje komponent.

records.context: A statistical detection sensitivity analysis needs a yes/no per simulated screening experiment before it can report a percentage. The model does not emit a yes/no — it emits a *ranking* of genes, scored by AUROC and average precision. So the screening experiment asks the user for the bar (``detection_auroc``, default 0.80) and reports the fraction of simulated screening experiments that clear it. Two things about that fraction are load-bearing:
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.power_design#12
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A power analysis needs a yes/no per simulated screen before it can report a percentage. The model does not emit a yes/no — it emits a *ranking* of genes, scored by AUROC and average precision. So the screen asks the user for the bar (``detection_auroc``, default 0.80) and reports the fraction of simulated screens that clear it. Two things about that fraction are load-bearing:
records.translation: En styrkeanalys behöver ett ja/nej per simulerad screen innan den kan rapportera en procentsats. Modellen ger inget ja/nej — den ger en *rangordning* av gener, poängsatt med AUROC och genomsnittlig precision. Därför ber skärmen användaren om ribban (``detection_auroc``, standard 0.80) och rapporterar andelen simulerade screens som klarar den. Två saker om den andelen är bärande:

records.context: 1. **Count failed or non-converged fits as non-detections.** Do not drop them: that would inflate statistical power by removing executions whose design was too weak to fit. 2. **Report mean AUROC beside statistical power.** Calculate the mean over converged fits and also report how many fits failed or did not converge. Thus power 0/5 with five non-converged fits differs from power 0/5 with five converged fits at AUROC 0.52.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.power_design#13
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. **A replicate whose fit failed or did not converge counts as a non-detection**, not as a missing value. Dropping it would raise the reported power by removing exactly the runs where the design was too thin to fit — which is the failure mode the analysis is supposed to find. 2. **The mean AUROC is reported beside the power**, over the replicates that did converge, with the count of those that did not. A power of 0/5 with five non-converged fits and a power of 0/5 with five converged fits at AUROC 0.52 are different findings.
records.translation: 1. **Ett replikat vars anpassning misslyckades eller inte konvergerade räknas som en icke-detektion**, inte som ett saknat värde. Att ta bort det skulle höja den rapporterade styrkan genom att ta bort just de körningar där designen var för tunn för att anpassas — vilket är det felläge som analysen ska hitta. 2. **Medelvärdet för AUROC rapporteras bredvid styrkan**, över de replikat som konvergerade, med antalet som inte gjorde det. En styrka på 0/5 med fem icke-konvergerade anpassningar och en styrka på 0/5 med fem konvergerade anpassningar vid AUROC 0.52 är olika fynd.

No image is opened, decoded or stacked to build that list. :func:`sample_image_sets` then draws a bounded random sample — 20 sets by default, adjustable from the :class:`FlatSpinBox` that sits immediately left of the sets dropdown.
records.translation: :func:`enumerate_image_sets` ersätter den. records.context: The panels rebuild their selectors on every image they load. Enumerating the folder each time is what made stepping through a large plate cost 292 ms a step, so the enumeration is done **once per folder** and every later call reuses it. Only :meth:`enumerate` touches the filesystem.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.preview_controls.ImageSetSampler#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The panels rebuild their selectors on every image they load. Enumerating the folder each time is what made stepping through a large plate cost 292 ms a step, so the enumeration is done **once per folder** and every later call reuses it. Only :meth:`enumerate` touches the filesystem.
records.translation: Panelerna bygger om sina väljare för varje bild de läser in. Att räkna upp mappen varje gång är det som gjorde att stegning genom en stor platta kostade 292 ms per steg, så uppräkningen görs **en gång per mapp** och varje senare anrop återanvänder den. Endast :meth:`enumerate` rör filsystemet.

records.context: Re-sampling is likewise deliberate: :meth:`sample` is a pure function of (folder, total, cap, nonce), so re-rendering after any settings change returns the identical sets. The sample changes only when the user changes the cap or calls :meth:`reshuffle`.

records.context: **Shared axes by default.** Two panels whose y axes differ by an order of magnitude look identical, so a per-panel autoscale turns "the knockdown halved the count" into "the two panels look the same". Every scale here is computed over the whole grid unless the user explicitly asks otherwise, and when they do ask otherwise :attr:`Trellis.notice` says so in words, so a free-scale trellis copied into a slide still states that its scales differ. :data:`SCALE_ROW` and :data:`SCALE_COL` are the middle grounds: panels down a column of the grid share, or panels across a row do, which is what you want when the rows are three different measurements and the columns are three conditions.

records.source: **Shared axes by default.** Two panels whose y axes differ by an order of magnitude look identical, so a per-panel autoscale turns "the knockdown halved the count" into "the two panels look the same". Every scale here is computed over the whole grid unless the user explicitly asks otherwise, and when they do ask otherwise :attr:`Trellis.notice` says so in words, so a free-scale trellis copied into a slide still states that its scales differ. :data:`SCALE_ROW` and :data:`SCALE_COL` are the middle grounds: panels down a column of the grid share, or panels across a row do, which is what you want when the rows are three different measurements and the columns are three conditions.
records.translation: **Gemensamma axlar som standard.** Två paneler vars y-axlar skiljer sig med en storleksordning ser identiska ut, så en automatisk skalning per panel gör "the knockdown halved the count" till "the two panels look the same". Varje skala här beräknas över hela rutnätet om inte användaren uttryckligen ber om något annat, och när användaren gör det säger :attr:`Trellis.notice` det med ord, så att ett trellis-diagram med fria skalor som kopieras till en bild ändå anger att dess skalor skiljer sig. :data:`SCALE_ROW` och :data:`SCALE_COL` är mellanvägarna: paneler nedåt i en kolumn i rutnätet delar, eller paneler längs en rad gör det, vilket är vad man vill ha när raderna är tre olika mätningar och kolumnerna är tre villkor.
